title: We built the Henry Labs brand, then carried it across every touchpoint.
description: PIXELUP LABS built the brand, website, partner dashboard and checkout for Henry Labs, a founding member of the Agentic Commerce Consortium.

hero.alt: We built the Henry Labs brand, then carried it across every touchpoint.

sections.heading: Why the brand was behind the company.

media.alt: Henry Labs wordmark over a blue and orange mountain landscape
Henry Labs positioning posters using the mountain imagery and angular brand mark

items.label: Where Henry Labs was
items.text: Henry Labs builds checkout for AI shopping apps. Visa had already cited their one-click checkout, and they were a founding member of the Agentic Commerce Consortium.

items.label: What the market looked like
items.text: Agentic commerce was filling up fast with startups that all sounded the same. Platforms choosing a checkout partner could not tell them apart.

items.label: How we found the gap
items.text: A competitor analysis and a product deep dive showed what Henry Labs really sells: an SDK platforms build on, not a shopping app.

items.label: Why it mattered
items.text: Platforms trust Henry Labs with their transactions and revenue. The company had earned that trust. The brand still looked early-stage.

sections.heading: Shoppers see the Henry button. Platforms sign the contract.

media.alt: Henry Labs execution layer positioning beside an illuminated shopping cart
Henry Labs identity and positioning presented on a large conference screen

items.label: Problem
items.text: Shoppers meet Henry Labs as a checkout button. Platforms meet it as infrastructure they trust with revenue. A shopper-first brand would look forgettable to the actual buyer.

items.label: Why it mattered
items.text: The founders wanted ethereal and technical, not consumer. Too soft reads like a shopping app. Too cold looks like every payments API.

items.label: What we did
items.text: We designed for the platform buyer first. Landscape imagery and a sunset palette carried the ethereal. Precise type, grids and real product UI carried the technical.

items.label: Outcome
items.text: One identity quiet enough to sit inside another company's checkout, and serious enough for a partner pitch.

sections.heading: Then the brand project turned into a product project.

media.alt: Henry Labs FigJam research board mapping partner and shopper personas
Henry Labs FigJam board mapping the audited checkout and shopper flows

items.label: Problem
items.text: A month into the brand work, Henry Labs asked us to design the product too: checkout and the partner dashboard, in a four-week sprint.

items.label: Why it mattered
items.text: Partners wanted sales, traffic and referrals at a glance. The old dashboard buried all three. Shoppers just wanted to buy.

items.label: What we did
items.text: We mapped both personas, audited the checkout flow and designed checkout first, handing it to their engineers mid-sprint.

items.label: Outcome
items.text: One design system, two hierarchies. Partners see revenue first. Shoppers see their cart.

sections.heading: One brand, three products.

media.alt: Henry Labs website hero 'Own your checkout.' over a glowing mountain landscape
Henry Labs website displayed on a laptop against a black and silver landscape
Henry Labs mobile features section on a phone framed by a torn chain-link fence
Henry Labs website feature section for building, monetizing and optimizing agentic commerce

paragraphs: The website, partner dashboard and consumer checkout all run on the same design system, so a shopper at checkout and a partner checking revenue are looking at the same company. The website tells the story in the order a buyer needs it: product data, universal cart, embedded checkout, then the analytics that come after.

sections.heading: In their own words.

media.alt: Henry Labs brand posters, positioning and website screens shown as one work wall

quote.text: PIXELUP LABS has been a great partner for us at Henry Labs. They handled our landing page redesign and core product design, and the output speaks for itself. Fast, thoughtful, and easy to work with. Highly recommend!

sections.heading: And this is where Henry Labs ended up.

media.alt: Henry Labs mobile website and brand mark over the launch landscape
Henry Labs website use cases displayed on a laptop against an orange landscape

paragraphs: Henry Labs now has a brand that looks as serious as the infrastructure behind it, a website that explains the product in the order buyers need it, and a design system its engineers build on directly.

The website went live in May 2026, and the checkout and dashboard were built in-house from our designs. Henry Labs CEO Phil Qiu shared it with one line: "We wanted a landing page that actually feels like that future rather than explaining it." By September, Henry Labs was powering Allowance (YC P26), which went from 9 to 90 stores in two weeks. You can see the live site at henrylabs.ai.

If you recognised Henry Labs' problem in your own company, we should talk. We work with AI and B2B SaaS teams on brand, web and product design, helping them look as credible as the product they have built.

title: We repositioned Streamline for enterprise, then scaled the brand across 200 pages.
description: PIXELUP LABS repositioned Streamline for enterprise legal teams and built a brand, website and design system that scaled across more than 200 pages.

hero.alt: Streamline serif wordmark over a collage of legal AI product cards with a woman working at a desk

sections.heading: Why the old brand was no longer a good fit.

media.alt: Streamline website collage with desktop homepage, mobile mockup, and integration tiles
Streamline 'Built for how modern legal teams work' website section on a green textured background

items.label: Where Streamline was
items.text: Streamline had a mature AI platform built for enterprise legal teams. The product was getting better and the company was moving into bigger accounts.

items.label: What the market looked like
items.text: When we looked at the competition, some newer competitors simply looked more modern, more credible and more enterprise-ready.

items.label: How we found the gap
items.text: We went deep into the business: a brand workshop with the team, a study of the competitive landscape, a map of their buyers, and time spent understanding the product.

items.label: Why it mattered
items.text: The gap became obvious. Their brand system was holding them back, and that mattered even more because Streamline was selling to Chief Legal Officers, General Counsels, legal ops teams and legal teams inside large companies.

sections.heading: Our first instinct was to make Streamline much bolder.

media.alt: Streamline document knowledge graph and Slack AI conversation cards on a green glass background
Streamline mobile integrations screen 'We work where your team already works'
Streamline integrations strip with Ironclad, Microsoft Teams, Slack, Salesforce, Jira, and DocuSign

items.label: Problem
items.text: If the old brand was underselling the product, the new one needed to make a much stronger statement. So we explored three creative directions: more colour, more gradients, more conceptual imagery, more personality.

items.label: Why it mattered
items.text: After the first round of feedback, we realised we had pushed too far. The new directions felt modern, but they no longer looked like a company built for enterprise legal teams. They were not lawyer-like.

items.label: What we did
items.text: The answer was not to make Streamline as different as possible. It was to make them feel modern without losing the trust their buyers expected. The question changed from how bold we could make Streamline to how modern we could make it without losing the maturity the product already had. The brief became: legal-tech serious, modern flavour.

items.label: Outcome
items.text: That principle guided every decision from there. Royal blue became the primary colour and leaf green the secondary. Neutrals did a lot of the work. Product and illustration supported the copy instead of overpowering it, and gradients and textures stayed but became more subtle.

sections.heading: Getting the brand right was only half the job.

items.label: Problem
items.text: Finding the right visual direction solved the perception problem. The next challenge was making it work across the entire website and every marketing touchpoint.

items.label: Why it mattered
items.text: Streamline did not need a five-page marketing site. The project grew to 40+ unique page designs, with the system extending across 200+ pages. A page written for a General Counsel had to tell a completely different story from an AI Contract Review page.

items.label: What we did
items.text: We turned the brand into a design system: reusable components, page structures, product templates, design rules and an illustration system that could stretch across the whole website. The illustrations had to support dozens of different ideas without making every page feel disconnected.

items.label: Outcome
items.text: By this point we were not just designing a new brand. We were building a system Streamline could keep using as the company grew.

sections.heading: One system, 200+ pages.

media.alt: Streamline 'Built for how modern legal teams work' team page on a tablet held in hands
Streamline resources section 'Insight for legal operations leaders' on a green background

paragraphs: Product, feature, industry, team and resource pages all run on the same components, so a General Counsel page and an AI Contract Review page can tell different stories without looking like different companies.

sections.heading: Results

media.alt: Streamline homepage hero 'In-house legal runs on Streamline' on a tablet held in hands

sections.heading: And this is where Streamline ended up.

media.alt: Streamline resources page on a laptop resting on a stone slab

paragraphs: Streamline had much more than a new homepage. They had a brand that finally matched the maturity of the product behind it, a design system that could extend across all the touchpoints, and a website built around the perception they needed with enterprise legal buyers.
After launch, the team also reported positive customer feedback and stronger enterprise conversations, including with Fortune 500 companies. You can see the live site at streamline.ai.
If you recognised Streamline's problem in your own company, we should talk. We work with AI and B2B SaaS teams on brand, web and product design, helping them move upmarket.
